fact.box: IREN Limited (NASDAQ: IREN), press release filed with the SEC on July 20, 2026
fact.claim: In July 2026 IREN raised its year-end 2026 AI cloud annualized run-rate revenue (ARR) target to more than $4bn, and said about 85% of it was already under multi-year contracts with AI developers worth $2.8bn in total. ARR is the company's own operating metric, not GAAP revenue. It assumes 480MW of AI cloud capacity gets built and accepted by customers by the end of 2026, so the revenue actually booked can come in much lower or later. The engine's 1-month chart supplies this month's price drop, and nothing here says what the stock will do next.

plain.what: IREN is a company that builds giant buildings full of computers that run AI, and rents that computing power to AI companies. In July 2026 it told the government it now aims for more than $4 billion a year from that AI renting business, and said about 85% of that amount is already covered by signed multi-year deals worth $2.8 billion. Its share price dropped 53.4% in one month, so the chart looks bad while the plan on paper looks big.
plain.so_what: That $4 billion is a target, not money in the bank, and it only happens if IREN finishes and gets customers to accept 480MW of computer capacity by the end of 2026.
plain.do: Write down the $4 billion target and the 480MW build, and check at IREN's next update whether the buildings are finished.
